title: BEVWorld: A Multimodal World Simulator for Autonomous Driving via Scene-Level BEV Latents

output_modality.value: camera plus lidar: future multi-view images and lidar point clouds rendered from predicted BEV latent tokens

control_signal.value: ego-motion action tokens (vehicle movement and steering), converted into left turn, right turn, speed up and slow down instructions

control_mechanism.value: action tokens modulate the input tokens of a spatial-temporal transformer that denoises future BEV tokens, with history BEV tokens as condition tokens; no classifier-free guidance used

base_model.value: Own multi-modal tokenizer (Swin-Transformer backbones, deformable fusion, NeRF-style ray rendering) plus latent BEV sequence diffusion model with spatial-temporal transformer, DDIM sampling; not built on a pretrained video backbone.

datasets.value: nuScenes (real) and Carla (simulated); Carla model fine-tuned from the nuScenes-pretrained model.

metrics.value: PSNR, FID, FVD, Chamfer distance (1s/3s); downstream 3D detection NDS/mAP and motion prediction minADE/minFDE for tokenizer pretraining.

controllability_evidence.value: Qualitative only: Figure 6 visualizes generations for turn left, turn right, speed up, slow down. No quantitative action-following metric in the packet.

closed_loop.value: No; open-loop future prediction up to 3 s (6 future frames) on nuScenes key frames.

stated_limitations.value: Diffusion inference needs about 50 steps, slow and costly; dynamic objects in images sometimes blurry, may need a dedicated module.

notes: Deliberately uses no manual layout or label conditions to stay scalable. Compares FID 19.0 and FVD 154.0 on nuScenes.
